# The Black Arks

*Pages PDF 14-19*

## **The Black Arks**
In the haze of smoke-filled taverns, where sailors gather to share tales of the sea, whispered stories of the black arks frighten even the briniest sea dogs. Coastal settlements across the world repeat the same dire legends of colossal citadels drifting ominously over the horizon, bringing ruin and terror to the helpless souls in their shadow. Every black ark carries a host of dark elves, roaming the oceans to sate their ambitions, reap captives, and carry the cold will of Malerion into every corner of the map. In their wake follows a hunting pack of lesser vessels, swift, barbed silhouettes crewed by the fleetmaster’s vassals, predatory corsairs who strike swiftly and stealthily. 

Each black ark is a singular abomination, its form and character indelibly marked by the sorcerous cabal that first wrenched it from the soil of Ulthuan. Of those original architects, most are long-dead, victims of centuries of warfare, murderous intrigues, and Malerion’s edict forbidding males from wielding magic. 

Over the long centuries, black arks have passed from hand to bloodstained hand, seized by ascendant noble houses who installed favoured fleetmasters in command. To be a fleetmaster is to rise high within dark elf society, though they must be careful to court the goodwill of the Dread King and obey Lord Venil Chillblade and Lady Drane Brackblood, two highborn Druchii to whom Malerion has entrusted the plundering of the world’s seas and coastlines. 

So it is that no ark remains static, as each successive fleetmaster reshapes their floating citadel, warping its battlements and halls to mirror their own cruelty, obsessions, and towering ambition. Some resemble great ships, with sculpted stone prows and soaring hulls, while others appear as islands of jagged Nagarythe bedrock, teeming with bastions and towers. Black arks vary greatly in size; _Tower of Midnight,_ for example, is the size of a small border fortress with a single tower, whereas _Fortress of Eternal Torture_ rivals the high elf city of Tor Koruali in its sprawling enormity. 

Few vessels can survive an encounter with a black ark. Their wake alone can capsize smaller ships and their battlements bristle with reaper bolt throwers, wicked artillery with a fearsome rate of fire. A naval engagement with a black ark is akin to besieging a fortress rather than attacking another ship. Most captains know to flee rather than fight, although even this does not guarantee survival, for despite their immense bulk, black arks are capable of an unsettling and unnatural speed. 

## **Notorious Black Arks**
_Palace of Oblivion._ in the years following the Sundering, _Palace of Oblivion_ proved a lynchpin of Malerion’s fleet. In −2425 IC, it became the first black ark to be sunk due to damage . it sustained after being rammed by the dragonship _Indraugnir_ 

_Citadel of Ecstatic Damnation_ and _Jade Palace of Pain_ . In −1599 IC, two arks were deliberately beached close to the site of Anlec in Nagarythe. They formed a fortified beachhead from which the dark elves assailed Ulthuan. In −696 IC, the dark elf force was finally repulsed, and the rebuilt Anlec, formed in the main part from the beached black arks, was torn down. 

_Talon of Agony_ . This mountainous black ark roved the eastern seas until 860 IC. Having filled its hold with plunder and captives taken from trading junks sailing from Wei-Jin, it was destroyed by a massive tidal wave. 

_Fortress of Eternal Torture_ . Commanded by Fleetmaster Maranith, who is also known as ‘Caledor’s Bane’ for his habit of fighting atop his dragon Wrath and slaying several high elven champions in aerial combat. 

_Black Serenade_ . Sailed into the Sapphire Gate of Lothern during the 2301 IC invasion of Ulthuan, and barely escaped after a frenzied dragon attack. 

_Tower of Blessed Dread_ . Commanded by the notorious Krakenlord Lokhir Fellheart, the most prolific and celebrated fleetmaster of the current era. 

The architecture of a black ark is a drifting reflection of Naggaroth itself. Soaring clusters of towers and narrow spires loom over the waves, while elegant crenelations line the dark stone walls, carved with elaborate patterns, baleful runes, and grotesque daemonic faces. Each ark mounts several tall masts, mounted with lateen sails, making for an incongruous sight amidst the fortress buildings. These propel the immense mass of the black ark through the ocean, augmented by ancient sorceries woven along lines of magical power within its bulk. Sorceresses tend these enchantments without cease, while shrouding their moving citadel in roiling banks of mist and weaving treacherous labyrinths of illusion to ensnare and confound any vessel that dares to draw close. 

Yet for all their size and power, black arks are not invulnerable. Many have been lost, either overrun by boarding armies, undone by treachery and sabotage, or sunk at great cost by fleets whose commanders possessed not only rare skill, but the grim persistence to hound a floating citadel to its death. 

The Temple of SpiTe 

## **History of Temple of Spite**
_Temple of Spite_ was once Athil Khairn, a fortress north of Athel Kanya in Nagarythe, and home to Lady Anethra Moonglade. A loyal follower of Morathi, the sorceress became a seeker of dark knowledge under her queen’s influence. She sided with Malerion in the elven civil war, adopting the epithet ‘Helbane’. When the Sundering devastated Ulthuan, she wrenched Athil Khairn from the land to escape the wrath of Phoenix King Caledor I. 

## **After the Sundering**
After months at sea, the black ark carried Anethra’s retainers to Naggaroth, where it witnessed the founding of Clar Karond. The fortress was renamed _Temple of Spite_ , and for centuries it prowled the oceans in service to Anethra and the lords of the nascent city alike.  The wealth and captives reaped during these voyages fed Anethra’s rising ambitions, allowing her to establish a dynasty whose shadow still looms large over the power and intrigues of Clar Karond. 

Successive fleetmasters have reshaped _Temple of Spite_ over the centuries, raising new towers, fortifications, and monuments to their cruelty. Under the draconian rule of Lord Valeth Helbane, a thousand wretches died building the formidable bastion and temple to Khaine known as Valeth’s Palace. New towers rose around the original keep of Athil Khairn, now the Fleetmaster’s Bastion, and were occupied by successful corsairs and highborn eager to stay close to their liege lord. 

In 2402 IC, _Temple of Spite_ sailed to the Chaos Wastes seeking to make strong thralls from the men of the northern tribes. During this mission the ark and its reavers clashed with a Chaos fleet under the daemon prince Lashscale. _Temple of Spite_ triumphed, and many marauders were shipped to Karond Kar’s markets, but they left behind a deadly legacy: a virulent daemonic plague that devastated the ark’s population for decades. 

In 2472 IC, _Temple of Spite_ launched a campaign against the high elven kingdom of Cothique, sending swift ravenships and doomreavers to attack vessels leaving the safety of the Shifting Isles. The Second Battle of Deloth’s Shoals saw two eagleships and eight hawkships sunk, and Princess Trasinaya of Tor Andar, who barely escaped with her life,  still harbours a special loathing for Duriath Helbane and his fleets. 

In 2485 IC, _Temple of Spite_ sent forth raiders to secure captives along the coast of the Empire. Captain Qulla’s raiders took captives from Broghur in Nordland, and Verborgenbucht and Zinnowitz in Ostland. 

In 2505 IC, Duriath informed the Council of Reavers of his plan to assault the high elf outpost of Tor Elithis. He declared his resolve to see every inhabitant taken in chains and raise a dark elf outpost on the ruins of the Asur settlement. Many denizens of the ark judged the scheme reckless in the extreme, for there was richer and far less perilous prey to be found. 

## **Mutiny on the Ark**
During the rule of fleetmaster Dravia Helbane, a colossal storm disrupted the flow of magic through the structure and seawater gushed into chambers below the waterline, threatening to sink the ark. Five sorceresses died as they wrangled tendrils of dark magic to keep the ark afloat, and some of the flooded caverns remain waterlogged to this day. 

## **Duriath Seizes Power**
In 2187 IC, Dravia fell victim to the calculated treachery of her cousin, Duriath Helbane, who lured her into joining a raid on an island off the Lustrian coast. In a single night of orchestrated slaughter, Duriath had her captains and retainers murdered and left Dravia marooned. Usurping the fleetmaster’s throne, he set about carving his name into history through a campaign of relentless persecution against the shipping of mankind. Thousands of human sailors were dragged away in chains or consigned to watery graves in service of Duriath’s mission. In Naggarond, Lady Drane Brackblood, who oversees the plundering of seas westward of Naggaroth, considered punishing Duriath for his treachery, but the new fleetmaster won such rich prizes that she was soon mollified. 

In 2507 IC, Captain Kranthar Mancleaver attempted a mutiny, backed by Death Hag Thakara of the Khainites and a substantial force from the warhost. They intended to slaughter Duriath and his supporters and seize control of the ark, but were betrayed by Captain Malida Redthorn. Kranthar and Thakara were torn apart, their corpses staked to the Fleetmaster’s Bastion and made carrion for harpies. An ensuing purge reduced the population of the black ark by almost a third, and whilst many of those executed were falsely accused by their enemies, a small faction of mutineers survived by concealing their part in the revolt. 

## **The Persistent Strain**
Deep in Valeth’s Palace is a doorway, bricked up and sealed with stone for over 100 years. Concealed within are the plagueridden corpses of a household: the family of Lady Hawkbane, castellan of the Fleetmaster’s Bastion. When she discovered her husband and children were infected with the daemonic plague, she ordered them sealed in a lightless room to die. While their bodies perished, their souls and the plague live on. 

## **Recent Voyages**
The attempted coup set back Helbane’s ambitions to take Tor Elithis. The fleetmaster has a new urgency to build up his warhost and find allies in Naggaroth. He commands his reavers to redouble their efforts in accumulating plunder and captives. 

## **To the East**
After Helbane spent a Season of Decadance courting the favour of Lord Venil Chillblade, _Temple of Spite_ was granted permission to reave the eastern oceans, moving north up the eastern coast of the Southlands where incursions inland brought the dark elves in conflict with the lizardmen of Teotiqua. A series of running battles amid the suffocating tangles of mangrove and reeking swamps deterred Helbane’s forces from further raids, though they secured several dozen gold plaques and mysterious items of considerable magical power. 

During 2508 IC, the ark menaced the coast of Ind, the high beastmaster eager to capture some of the rare and exotic creatures of that land. After many months raiding the steaming jungles in blistering heat, an expedition of Captain Yrmaldrel Manbane and the beastmasters dragged a strange tigerheaded beastman onto the vessel, and the forlorn creature still languishes in the menagerie. 

_Temple of Spite_ next sailed southeast towards the Gates of Calith, where high elf outposts dispatched squadrons of swift eagleships and the dragonship _Celestial Spear_ to harry the black ark. The Asur forces sank six ravenships and lost a single eagleship in return, as the _Temple of Spite_ made haste to the Far Sea. 

## **Gates of Calith**
Between the southern tip of Khuresh and the Southern Wastes is a narrow strait, the Gates of Calith. Elven fortresses stand on both sides of the strait to control sea traffic between Lustria and the lands to the west. Passage through the gates is difficult for a large fleet or a black ark, though individual ships can slip past if they are swift enough. 

Stewardship of the gates falls to high mage Torinubar, chosen for his mastery of magic that repels the influence of Chaos. The southern fortress is forever at risk of corruption from the polluted southern wastes, where daemons and beastfiends cavort and threaten the bastion. 

Calith’s naval patrols and garrison are hardened veterans, each elf tested for mental stability and resilience in the face of the horrors beyond the walls. In recent years, a large force of skaven assaulted the northern fortress by land and sea. The elves sank the ratmen’s ramshackle ships and the verminous armies scurried back to their masters. 

The Temple of SpiTe 

## **Sailing the Sea of Dread**
As the ark passed north along the coast of Khuresh, sorceress Xalthea Nightwind informed Helbane that the Blood Naga of Khuresh are renowned for their cruelty and cunning, and would make fine allies in an attack on Tor Elithis. The Black Convocation sent emissaries across the Marble Mountains to treat with the Naga Queens, yet nothing was heard of the party again and no message came from the rulers of Khuresh. 

In spring 2509 IC, a warhost made landfall on the south-east coast of Grand Cathay, where they allied with a bandit warlord in attacking the local Lord Magistrate’s forces. They were promised a rich reward, but Lord Tualarc, commander of the ark’s warhost, elected to betray the warlord, taking prisoners and two captured warships back to _Temple of Spite_ . 

## _**Temple of Spite**_ **at Bay**
Far from Naggarond, Duriath feared venturing into the seas overseen by Lady Brackblood, whose favour he neglected in recent decades. As the Dragon Emperor of Grand Cathay assembled a fleet in response to Lord Tualarc’s actions, Helbane defied the wishes of the Council of Reavers and refused to engage with them. He elected instead to send ships to scout Tor Elithis. When the corsairs returned, they confirmed that _Temple of Spite_ lacked sufficient force to take the high elf outpost. Helbane resolved to return to Naggaroth to exchange loot and captives for ships and troops. 

## **Tor Elithis**
The isles of elithis lie at the edge of the oceans, a mysterious archipelago unexplored beyond the high elves’ sole outpost. Tor elithis occupies an important strategic location between the Gates of Calith and the west coast of Lustria. 

High elves docking at Tor Elithis’ ancient port experience a cloying sense of unease, as if the colony is somehow ill-fated. The seeress ingmir has foreseen the city’s fate, a vision of daemonic hordes surging from the Southern Wastes to possess every soul found within the walls. Though her prophecy stirs fear among the colonists, Ingmir remains resolute. She has sent word to Ulthuan that she and her council intend a perilous exodus, seeking to preserve the souls of the resident Asur rather than leave them to the inevitable corruption and death foretold by her visions. 

Duriath Helbane and his command know nothing of Ingmir’s prophecies. As far as they are concerned the high elves of Tor Elithis have no reason to expect danger. 

## **To the West**
_Temple of Spite_ sailed into the Great Ocean, skirting far south of the Citadel of Dusk, and as the ark progressed north towards Naggaroth, corsair captains made opportunistic attacks on human and elven ships off the coast of Lustria. In 2510 IC, _Temple of Spite_ overwintered off Karond Kar and traded much of its best plunder there before sailing for its home city of Clar Karond when the seas thawed in spring. 

For several months, the inhabitants of the ark went about their business in the city, trading, scheming, and carousing with the proceeds of years’ raiding. During this time, Fleetmaster Helbane and his trusted retainers conspired with Lady Anethra Helbane, talking of ambition and the assault on Tor Elithis. Whilst many corsairs and warriors joined the ark, it was not enough for the Helbanes’ liking, and they lacked the confidence to assault the high elves whilst _Temple of Spite_ was undermanned. 

Since setting forth from Karond Kar in summer 2511 IC, _Temple of Spite_ has haunted the seas around the Old World. Several raiding ships braved the mists around Albion, drawn by tales of sea elf renegades claiming that the humans there were easily fooled and ancient ruins harboured treasures far inland. The more daring captains made landfall and returned to the ark with captives and strange tales of rock-throwing giants, vast circular earthworks, and great stone henges. 

Off the Norscan coast, the ark was attacked by Graeling longships, the frenzied Norscans sealing their own doom, though some marauders successfully scaled the walls. Several corsair crews set out to trade exotic goods with the wood elves at Se-Athil on Wreckers’ Point and the Bjornling port of Skjold. The ark then turned southeast into the Sea of Claws, returning once again to menace shipping around the coasts of Bretonnia, the Wasteland, and the Empire. 

## **The Saga of Thraeg Icejaw**
Thraeg Icejaw fought like a daemon as his tribesmen fell to the quick blades of Captain Delekth’s corsairs. The reavers threw nets over the Norscan to capture him alive and now Thraeg is Delekth’s property, an especially belligerent thrall of prodigious strength and cunning. On occasion, Delekth orders the Norscan brought from the cells to fight in the arena as his champion. If the dark elves knew of Thraeg’s new mutation, they would ensure he does not survive the next fight. With a little time and effort, he makes his bones alter shape, growing long and slender or stout and short, so escaping his confinement is trivial. Several Norscans, Kislevites, and Albion captives have pledged to fight with him when he chooses his moment.
